The story I had in mind goes like this:

Two Kingdoms have coexisted peacefully for hundreds of years, Trade flourishing betweeen them. The capital city of one kingdom lies at the mouth of the great river, just where the great swamp starts (I have no names yet, this is where I need help.) This kingdom is culturally like medieval dutch/german culture, with a king and a council and courts and a strong set of laws and many soldiers and officers to enforce those laws. Most power and wealth is concentrated in the main city. Think Imperials.

The other kingdom is located in the highlands in the east of the map. They are culturally more like Vikings, strong, independent and tribal, with a King/thane/whatever ruling. The main city doesn't stand out much from the other villages, except for the King's castle.

It comes to pass that a merchant in the imperial Kingdom becomes so wealthy that he lends money to the King (and to other surrounding implied Kingdoms) and through that gains almost complete control over the Kingdom. The Viking King refuses to borrow and become enslaved, so the merchant hatches a plan. A village from the imperial kingdom is attacked and burnt to the ground, all inhabitants gruesomely killed and made it all to look like the vikings attacked. The imperial peasants upon hearing this of course rally for war, fueled by fiery speeches from the King and his Dukes. In the Viking Kingdom people are outraged and upset with the King that he would order such an atrocity. Tensions arise within the population and the Kingdom threatens to split.

This is the backstory, the player starts as the daughter/son of a blacksmith in an imperial village. Soldiers of the King show up one day and demand your father make weapons for the coming war for almost no compensation. When your father refuses he is hauled off to jail under trumped up charges.

That's how far I got with the story, I thought the player would of course try to get the father out of jail and in the course uncover the whole plot and be the hero. I also need a lot of sidequests and just general lore, e.g. for books.
